title: Cron engine: normalize collapses fields with a step
statement:
# Timezone-less cron engine (`src/cron.mjs`)

Module that interprets 5-field cron expressions and computes occurrences. Instants are objects `{ year, month, day, hour, minute }` of integers (month 1–12, day 1–31, hour 0–23, minute 0–59), with no seconds nor time zone; the calendar is proleptic Gregorian (leap year: divisible by 4 and not by 100, or divisible by 400).

Users report that `normalize('*/15 9-17 * * MON-FRI')` returns `'* 9-17 * * 1-5'` instead of `'0,15,30,45 9-17 * * 1-5'`. The whole module must obey the contract below.

## Syntax

Expression = 5 fields separated by one or more spaces/tabs (surrounding whitespace is ignored), in this order:

| field | name (`field`) | accepted values | `*` covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| minute | `minute` | 0–59 | 0–59 |
| hour | `hour` | 0–23 | 0–23 |
| day of month | `dayOfMonth` | 1–31 | 1–31 |
| month | `month` | 1–12 or `JAN`…`DEC` | 1–12 |
| day of week | `dayOfWeek` | 0–7 or `SUN`…`SAT` (0 and 7 = Sunday) | 0–6 |

Each field is a comma-separated list of items; each item is `*`, `N` or `N-M` (inclusive), optionally followed by `/S` (integer step ≥ 1, counted from the start of the range). `*/S` walks the range covered by `*`; `N/S` is equivalent to `N-X/S`, where X is the largest value covered by `*` in that field. Names are valid only in their own field, case-insensitive, and may appear in ranges (`MON-FRI`). In the day of week, the value 7 is converted to 0 **after** expansion (`5-7` → {0, 5, 6}).

Errors throw `CronError` (exported, subclass of `Error`) with the property `field` equal to the name of the problematic field: value out of range or not recognized, range with start greater than end (including `N/S` with N greater than X, e.g. `7/1` in the day of week), step 0 or non-numeric, empty item (`1,,2`), more than one `-` or `/` in the item. Number of fields other than 5 (including the empty string) → `CronError` with `field === null`. Expression that is not a string → `TypeError`.

## API

- `parse(expr)` → `{ minute, hour, dayOfMonth, month, dayOfWeek }`, each one `{ restricted, values }`: `values` are the allowed values, without repetition, in ascending order; `restricted` is `false` **only** when the field text is exactly `*` — any other form (`*/1`, `*/2`, `1-31`…) is restricted.
  - `parse('10-50/20 * * * *').minute.values` → `[10, 30, 50]`; `parse('* * * * 1/2').dayOfWeek.values` → `[1, 3, 5]`.
- **Day rule**: if `dayOfMonth` and `dayOfWeek` are both restricted, a day matches when it matches **either** of the two (OR); otherwise, the day must match both (which, in practice, applies only the restricted field). Minute, hour and month must always match.
  - `'0 0 13 * FRI'` fires on Fridays **and** on every 13th; `'0 0 */10 * MON'` fires on days 1, 11, 21, 31 **and** on Mondays; `'0 12 1 * *'` only on day 1.
- `matches(expr, t)` → boolean.
- `next(expr, from)` → first occurrence **strictly after** `from`; `prev(expr, from)` → last one **strictly before**. The search examines days up to the year `from.year + 100` inclusive (in `prev`, down to the year `max(1, from.year - 100)` inclusive); no occurrence within that reach → `null` (e.g.: `'0 0 30 2 *'`, `'0 0 31 4,6,9,11 *'`). Months without the requested day are skipped.
  - `next('0 0 31 * *', {2025,1,31,0,0})` → 2025-03-31 00:00; `next('0 0 29 2 *', {2025,3,1,0,0})` → 2028-02-29 00:00.
- `nextN(expr, from, n)` → array with the next `n` chained occurrences (fewer, if the search returns `null`); `n` must be an integer ≥ 0, otherwise `RangeError`.
- `between(expr, from, to, limit = 1000)` → occurrences `t` with `from < t <= to`, in order, at most `limit` (integer ≥ 0, otherwise `RangeError`).
- `normalize(expr)` → canonical form with 5 fields separated by one space: unrestricted field → `*`; restricted field → its `values` in order, with each run of **3 or more** consecutive integers written as `a-b` and the others separated by commas (day of week already with 7 converted to 0).
  - `normalize('1,2,3,5,6 * */1 JAN,FEB *')` → `'1-3,5,6 * 1-31 1,2 *'`; `normalize('0 0 * * 5-7')` → `'0 0 * * 0,5,6'`.
- Also exported: `isLeapYear`, `daysInMonth`, `dayOfWeek` (0 = Sunday), `compareTime(a, b)` and `SEARCH_YEARS = 100`.

Received instants are validated: integer fields, year 1–9999, existing date (e.g.: 2025-02-29 is invalid), hour 0–23, minute 0–59; violation → `RangeError` (missing object → `TypeError`). In `nextN`/`between`, the expression is validated before the instants. The functions never change the received objects and always return new objects.

bugs.summary: parseField marks the field as unrestricted when the text starts with '*' (e.g.: '*/2'), instead of only when it is exactly '*'; affects normalize and the OR rule of day of month/day of week
